evidence: Systemic: numerous ENABLED, visible Reality-Android controls are wired to empty placeholder lambdas (`onClick = { /* ... */ }`), so tapping them does nothing - a reachable completeness gap across shipped screens. These are call-site onClicks, not composable default params.

AccountScreen.kt: compare (line 449), privacy (465), about (474), avatar/preference picker rows (652,659,666,673), terms (737), privacy policy (743), help (749), feedback (755) - ~10 dead rows/buttons on the signed-in account screen.

AgencyInquiriesScreen.kt: batch-reply (89) and search (120); ListingAnalyticsScreen.kt: share (58); SearchScreen.kt: save-search (373, `/* opens KmpSaveSearchModal (deferred) */`).

Distinct from the already-filed nearby-tab-placeholder (ListingDetailTabs.kt) and create-listing-stub (Navigation.kt).

mobile-native/androidApp/src/main/java/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/ui/auth/TwoFactorScreen.kt:164 - the 'Use backup code' affordance (TextButton rendering stringResource(R.string.auth_2fa_backup_code)) is wired to `onClick = { /* backup code */ }`, an empty placeholder.

Impact: on the 2FA challenge screen a user who has lost access to their TOTP authenticator has NO working in-app recovery path - the backup-code button is visible and tappable but does nothing, which can lock a legitimate user out of their account.

Fix: wire the button to a backup-code entry flow (dialog/sub-screen) that posts the recovery code to the reality-server 2FA verify endpoint; confirm a backup/recovery-code verify endpoint exists in the auth spec before landing, and add a happy-path + invalid-code test. Worst instance of the dead-placeholder-button class, filed separately for its account-recovery severity.
